business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Shiprocket is a merchant-first, API-led technology platform that enables e-commerce transactions for India's MSMEs and Large Retailers (retailers with more than Rs 2,500 million of revenue per annum), principally those selling direct-to-consumer through their own websites, apps or social channels ("Direct Commerce"). Its Core Business aggregates third-party logistics providers for domestic shipping and layers value-added Shipping Apps on top (NDR panel, weight management, COD remittance, AI-based EDD prediction at 78.51% accuracy in Fiscal 2026); its Emerging Business adds cargo and fulfilment (including Shiprocket Omuni), cross-border shipping (ShiprocketX/CargoX), ads and checkout (Fastrr), capital solutions and hyperlocal delivery (Shiprocket Quick). The Company owns no delivery fleet and no fulfilment infrastructure of consequence, serving 214,769 Active Merchants in Fiscal 2026 through more than 250 ecosystem partners.

- Logibricks Technologies Private Limited — Associate company: CIN U74999PN2017PTC168376; registered office at Baner, Pune
- Group Companies — None: "As of date of this Red Herring Prospectus, our Company does not have any Group Company."
- Promoter — None: "OUR COMPANY IS PROFESSIONALLY MANAGED AND DOES NOT HAVE AN IDENTIFIABLE PROMOTER" - no identifiable promoter in terms of the SEBI ICDR Regulations and the Companies Act, 2013

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Core Business:** Domestic Shipping platform - logistics provider aggregation across 42 active courier partners with AI-based partner recommendation, NDR (non-delivery report) panel with address-score intelligence and escalation APIs, Weight Management System, including Weight Freeze and Zero Weight Discrepancy Guarantee Program, COD remittance cycle independent of logistics providers' remittance process, EDD prediction system (78.51% accuracy in Fiscal 2026), also exposed via API, Shipping Apps - instant pickups, order tracking, Shiprocket Secure, RTO Score, RTO Suit, Delivery Boost, Brand Boost, Notify, Instant COD, early COD remittance
- **Emerging Business:** Cargo - partial truckload and full truckload heavy logistics aggregation within India, Fulfilment - merchant inventory storage and order processing across leased fulfilment centres, Shiprocket Omuni - unified commerce platform connecting marketplaces, brand websites and physical retail stores, ShiprocketX - cross-border parcel platform with customs clearance and overseas delivery, CargoX - international door-to-door B2B / bulk air cargo, Shiprocket Ads and Marketing Solutions, including Engage360 remarketing, Fastrr Checkout - one-click checkout with single sign-on, fraud prevention and COD-to-prepaid conversion, Shiprocket Fintech - business loans and credit lines originated through 13 NBFC and lending partners in Fiscal 2026, Shiprocket Quick - on-demand hyperlocal same-day intra-city delivery on an aggregator model, Shiprocket Trends (currently free) and Shiprocket Sense - merchant data-insight platforms, Shiprocket Co-Pilot - AI merchant support tool

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Asset-light aggregator / platform model with no backward or forward integration into physical logistics: the Company owns no delivery fleets and no fulfilment centres, and operates entirely out of leased premises and co-working spaces. Third-party logistics partners (42 active courier partners as of March 31, 2026), fulfilment centre providers, communication platforms, shopping carts, marketplaces, payment gateways, ERPs, developers and credit providers are integrated via APIs into an ecosystem of more than 250 partners from April 2021 to March 2026. Contracts with logistics partners are on an independent-contractor, non-exclusive basis, typically long-term and remaining in force until terminated by either side, with standard pricing by weight and delivery area plus insurance and indemnity provisions. Despite the outsourced supply, the Company runs a 'full-responsibility model', taking complete ownership of platform transactions from fulfilment to payments and post-order processes, including escalating complaints, handling operational lapses and absorbing financial losses arising from shipments; COD remittance to Merchants runs on a cycle independent of the logistics providers' own remittance process. Forward extensions are software-led rather than physical: Fastrr Checkout at the front of the order journey, Engage360/ads at demand generation, Shiprocket Fintech (13 NBFC and lending partners in Fiscal 2026, bilateral lending directly between partner and Merchant) for working capital, and Shiprocket Quick as an aggregator-model hyperlocal layer. Physical footprint is limited to 13 leased fulfilment centres (762,826 sq ft across 10 cities), warehouse management at 5 customer-owned fulfilment centres and 11 third-party-operated warehouses. Inorganic build-out rather than integration: Glaucus (February 2022), Pickrr (June 2022, fully integrated in Fiscal 2024), Shiprocket Omuni (October 2022) and Swiftly/Wigzo (December 2021, marketing-automation tool acquired September 2023 and stake sold); goodwill impairments of ₹1,246.41 million (Shiprocket Omuni) and ₹521.01 million (Swiftly/Wigzo) were taken as exceptional items in Fiscal 2024. In Fiscal 2026 the Company made an investment in a company providing storage, warehousing and logistics services.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Cost of Merchant Solutions - what Shiprocket pays its logistics and ecosystem partners - is the dominant cost line at 69.39%, 69.34% and 58.94% of total expenses in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, so gross economics are set by partner rate negotiation rather than by owned assets
- Two-speed segment mix: Adjusted EBITDA - Core Business of Rs 1,866.37 million (12.56% margin) in Fiscal 2026 against Adjusted EBITDA - Emerging Business of Rs (1,689.89) million ((31.37)% margin); consolidated Adjusted EBITDA is only Rs 176.48 million (0.87%)
- Contribution Margin as a % of Revenue from Operations was 18.34%, 18.77% and 15.00% in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 - Core Business steady around 21% while Emerging Business improved to 10.55% from 1.47% over Fiscal 2024 to Fiscal 2026
- Fiscal 2024's Rs 5,951.81 million loss was driven by overlapping overhead from integrating acquired entities plus exceptional impairment of goodwill and other intangibles from the Pickrr and Shiprocket Omuni acquisitions; operational synergies from Fiscal 2024 onwards cut losses sharply thereafter
- Operating cash flow inflected: net cash from operating activities of Rs 526.37 million and Rs 18.97 million in Fiscals 2026 and 2025 against Rs (2,159.92) million used in Fiscal 2024
- Working capital runs on a negative cash conversion cycle - (10.34), (29.22) and (35.71) days in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 - funded by Merchant wallet balances, but the cycle has narrowed toward zero over three years
- Unit economics improving on both sides: Core Business CAC fell to Rs 2,829.31 from Rs 4,101.24 while Power Merchant ARPU rose to Rs 1.78 million from Rs 1.28 million between Fiscals 2024 and 2026; revenue per employee rose to Rs 14.77 million from Rs 10.18 million
- Merchant acquisition is shifting channel: Emerging Business supplied 20.98% of new Active Merchants in Fiscal 2026 versus 6.23% in Fiscal 2024, with 23,683 new Emerging Business Merchants added in Fiscal 2026
- Merchant compensation for lost, damaged or stolen shipments and proof-of-delivery disputes rose to Rs 531.11 million in Fiscal 2026 from Rs 280.32 million in Fiscal 2024; the RHP states this is recovered in full from logistics partners so no net loss is absorbed
- Receivables quality: trade receivables of Rs 2,878.77 million as of March 31, 2026 of which Rs 513.82 million are credit-impaired, plus Rs 1,499.10 million of unbilled revenue
- Balance sheet: total borrowings of the Company were Rs 2,445.03 million as on July 10, 2026, of which Rs 2,100.00 million is earmarked for repayment/prepayment from Net Proceeds in Fiscal 2027

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Retain and grow the Merchant base - expand product coverage across payments, capital, shipping and fulfilment, cross-sell into the existing base, and lift revenue per Merchant and transaction volumes to improve unit economics
- Deepen penetration in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities and among semi-digital Merchants, opening new regional offices in Western and Southern India in addition to the existing eight regional offices
- Grow Domestic Shipping and Shipping Apps, adding more quick shipping modes (same-day, next-day) and new shipping categories such as specialised logistics and return management
- Continuously expand product offerings and drive cross-sales into higher-margin services - BNPL, dynamic pricing, payment failovers, loyalty integrations and personalised product suggestions at checkout, AI-powered ad optimisation and premium logistics provider integration
- Invest in the Emerging Business to expand TAM - new cross-border trading lanes to the Middle East, Australia and Canada, wider U.K. and Middle East coverage, offshore warehousing, return inventory management and forward placement, express services, and bulk/cargo export categories
- Expand hyperlocal delivery by partnering with dark-store networks and building a last-mile partner fleet of bikes, light commercial vehicles and three-wheelers
- Strengthen the ecosystem organically and inorganically - grow the partner network, add integrations (payment gateways, loyalty providers, shopping carts, ERPs, shipping partners, lenders) and continue the acquisition track record (Glaucus, Pickrr, RocketBox, Swiftly, Shiprocket Omuni)
- Continue investing in data and AI - build generative AI bots over text and voice for service, account management and onboarding; monetise the currently free Shiprocket Trends insights platform as a paid product and scale Shiprocket Sense
- Scale partnerships with Merchant-focused organisations such as cooperatives and rural distribution networks, plus a referral and affiliate programme to create organic acquisition loops

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Shiprocket has no manufacturing footprint - the model is explicitly asset-light, with no owned delivery fleets and no owned fulfilment centres. Physical expansion is therefore leasehold and network-shaped: 13 leased fulfilment centres across 10 cities plus warehouse-management mandates at 5 customer-owned fulfilment centres and 11 third-party-operated warehouses as of March 31, 2026; eight regional offices, with new regional offices planned in Western and Southern India to reach Tier 2 and Tier 3 Merchants in person. Cross-border expansion is the most concrete build-out: five lanes from India to the U.S., U.K., Canada, Europe and Singapore serving 146 countries in Fiscal 2026 through 21 supply chain partners, with stated plans to set up new lanes to the Middle East, Australia and Canada, deepen U.K. and Middle East coverage, extend first-mile pickup to more cities, establish offshore warehousing facilities, and open new categories such as jewellery, pharmaceuticals, heavy goods and premium products. Hyperlocal (Shiprocket Quick) launched in Q2 Fiscal 2025, first earned revenue in Q4 Fiscal 2025 and covered 92 cities in Fiscal 2026, with expansion planned via dark-store partnerships and a last-mile partner fleet. The funded portion of this is Rs 3,656.00 million of Net Proceeds into marketing and technology for the platforms across Fiscals 2027 to 2029, weighted 67.90% to the Emerging Business; the RHP describes no plant, capacity or commissioning programme of any kind.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Profitable and scalable Core Business with operating leverage - Core Business profitable since Fiscal 2022; Revenue from Operations - Core Business grew at a 17.02% CAGR from Fiscal 2024 to Fiscal 2026 with Adjusted EBITDA - Core Business rising to Rs 1,866.37 million (12.56% margin) in Fiscal 2026
- Asset-light structure - no owned delivery fleets or fulfilment centres; gross additions to property, plant and equipment were only 0.88%, 0.34% and 2.25% of Revenue from Operations in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, with a negative cash conversion cycle of (10.34) days in Fiscal 2026
- Expanding platform network effects - data from more than 155 million end consumers and more than 730 million unique transactions processed between October 2016 and March 2026 feed AI models (RTO high-risk identification at 83.01% accuracy, 92.83% of checkout addresses pre-filled in Fiscal 2026)
- Leveraging scale - largest new-age end-to-end horizontal e-commerce enablement platform in India by revenue from operations in Fiscal 2026 and largest Merchant base among such platforms with revenue above Rs 1 billion (Redseer Report); same-day delivery in 34 cities and next-day delivery in 530 cities in Fiscal 2026
- Self-serve platform drawing organic traffic - 96.73% of Core Business Merchant onboarding completed without support-team intervention and an average 2.34 million monthly visitors in Fiscal 2026, holding Core Business CAC down to Rs 2,829.31 from Rs 4,101.24 in Fiscal 2024
- Diversified Merchant base minimising revenue concentration - top 1, 5 and 20 Merchants at 2.83%, 7.43% and 17.65% of Fiscal 2026 Revenue from Operations; top 250 Power Merchants include Mamaearth, boAt, Levis, Bata and Blackberrys
- Full transaction accountability - Shiprocket acts as the trust layer, compensating Merchants for lost, damaged or stolen shipments and SLA breaches (Rs 531.11 million paid in Fiscal 2026) and stating it recovers such amounts in full from logistics partners; 344 Key Account Managers as of March 31, 2026
- Cross-sell depth - 75.48% of Power Merchants used more than two products and 58.32% more than three products in Fiscal 2026; Power Merchant ARPU rose to Rs 1.78 million from Rs 1.28 million in Fiscal 2024
- Modular and open platform - API-first design allowing third-party developers to extend functionality, supporting rapid acquisition and integration of new capabilities
- Experienced leadership team and strong corporate governance - CEO Saahil Goel with 21 years of e-commerce experience and with the Company since 2011; CFO Kumar Tanmay with the Company since 2021; board of seven with four Independent Directors

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Loss-making at the consolidated level in every disclosed year, with no stated path or date to profitability — Restated Loss for the year of Rs 792.45 million, Rs 744.49 million and Rs 5,951.81 million in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 (3.91%, 4.56% and 45.23% of Revenue from Operations). Basic and diluted EPS were negative in all three years, so no P/E can be struck against earnings; the RHP itself flags that losses may continue.
- The Emerging Business is structurally loss-making yet absorbs the bulk of the growth capital — Adjusted EBITDA - Emerging Business was Rs (1,689.89) million in Fiscal 2026 on a (31.37)% margin, and it consumed the Core Business's Rs 1,866.37 million of Adjusted EBITDA almost entirely. 67.90% of the Rs 3,656.00 million platform-investment object is earmarked for this segment, so consolidated profitability depends on a segment that has never been profitable.
- Extreme dependence on non-exclusive third-party logistics partners — The top five active couriers carried 84.50% of total shipment volume in Fiscal 2026 (149.13 million shipments) out of 42 active courier partners. Contracts are non-exclusive, terminable, and the same partners could expand into Shiprocket's own platform features; there is no owned fleet to fall back on.
- Pass-through cost structure leaves little margin buffer — Cost of Merchant Solutions was 69.39% of total expenses in Fiscal 2026 (Rs 14,941.29 million on Rs 20,241.41 million of revenue). Any adverse move in logistics-partner rates flows almost directly to a consolidated Adjusted EBITDA margin of just 0.87%.
- Consumption-based revenue is hostage to Merchants' own trading and traffic — Revenue moves with the Merchants' sales volumes, which the Company explicitly states are beyond its control; service agreements are typically indefinite with no committed volumes, so a downturn in Merchant demand or a shift back toward marketplaces passes straight through.
- Acquisition and impairment track record, with more unidentified inorganic growth planned — Fiscal 2024's loss was materially driven by exceptional impairment of goodwill and other intangibles arising from the Pickrr and Shiprocket Omuni acquisitions plus overlapping integration overhead. The Company intends to fund further acquisitions from Net Proceeds with no target identified and no definitive agreement in place.
- No identifiable promoter combined with wide, unappraised discretion over Net Proceeds — The Company is professionally managed with no identifiable promoter and no Group Company. Funding requirements were not appraised by any bank, financial institution or independent agency, and up to 35% of Gross Proceeds may go to unidentified acquisitions and general corporate purposes together (up to 25% individually).
- Auditor emphasis of matter and recurring audit-trail modifications — The Statutory Auditors reported an emphasis of matter for Fiscal 2024, and modifications under the Report on Other Legal and Regulatory Requirements relating to daily backup of books of account and audit trail for all three of Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 - a books-and-records control weakness that persisted through the IPO year.
